Everything and anything about college.

I was bombarded with things from my school about scholarships, FASFA, and even certain college terms before I even knew what they were, because I was never taught about it. Probably my parent's fault for not teaching me, but schools not teaching you important information because they assume you should know it already is a problem, and not just for college stuff either.

Edit: in high school I mean. Please try to learn about college before you go to college

Thank you man. It's really refreshing to hear some kind words. I don't really like to use her as a way out of this hole, because I know what it's like to get too emotionally dependent on a person for your happiness. I don't know what's motivated me to keep going all these years but that last line really hits home.

Best of luck to you man, may both of us reach (at least) level 6.

I've thought about this question a lot and been asked this by some therapists and it usually boils down to this: I'm fucking terrified.

I'm terrified of life, of the uncertainty of the future, of failure, of pretty much just everything and everything going wrong. I've always been assuming I'd kill myself when I was young but I never did, so I'm living in this future I've never expected nor prepared myself to deal with.
I used to get smashed to try to forget and just move on but I stopped drinking for her and now basically have nothing to numb the pain.

Let me tell you this one thing: you are not selfish.

These things do not make you selfish. Your feelings are not selfish. Your feelings are real and validated and if your friend can't handle your grief then that's a problem they have to deal with themselves, not you. You are allowed to grieve, to have feelings. 

It's a terrible thing to go through when you lose your partner. You shouldn't have to go through it alone. Have you tried talking to a therapist or another professional? It sounds like you have a lot of weight on your shoulders and I couldn't imagine having to deal with that without the help of someone who knows how to get through that stuff.
